It's an extremely tough industry. The sheer amount of good indie games that get released every week create so much competition for our limited game time and wallets that even price becomes a factor, of all things. You'd think that quality would matter first, but quality is partly subjective. Every purchase is a risk, and a lower price means a lesser loss if it turns out to be a bad purchase.

Personally I stopped caring about prices when I started earning an income, which incidentally also coincided with the moment I stopped having a lot of free time. For me and most active adult gamers I suppose, games that are good can be costly, even if short.

That's a really good point. I worry that low-price/low-effort games hurt the industry in a few ways, by flooding the market with low quality games and by skewing our perception of how much a good game should cost. Why pay $20 for a good game when I can get these 16 games for $5, even if I never play them much at all? If every game cost more (low effort or not), then it would mean turning down more games, but that would also mean I might put more thought into whether a game is going to occupy my time or not. Ultimately, I think the problem is not that I can get 16 low-effort games for $5, but more that I don't put enough thought into how those nickles and dimes add up, and appreciate that sometimes a good game is worth the price if it gives me as much entertainment as a dozen mediocre games.
